Salam Patwary (born 8 May 1966) is a Bangladeshi academic and senior political leader. Holding three PhDs and recognized as the first Bangladeshi mariner to achieve a doctorate, Patwary reached the upper echelons of the ruling party, serving as a Vice President of the Central Committee of the Bangladesh Awami League.
Academic Career
Patwary is noted for a distinguished academic record, holding three PhD degrees in the following fields:
* Criminology and Victimology
* Social Welfare
* Islamic Studies
A graduate of the 3rd intake of the Bangladesh Marine Academy, he holds the distinction of being the first mariner in national history to attain a PhD degree. He has held professorships or senior teaching roles at the University of Dhaka, North South University, and Stamford University Bangladesh.
Advocacy for Hawker's Rights
Patwary is widely recognized for his foundational role in organizing the informal labor sector in Dhaka:
* Bangladesh Awami Hawkers League: He founded the Bangladesh Awami Hawkers League to formally establish and protect the legal and economic rights of street vendors. Under his leadership, the League advocated for permanent rehabilitation and protections against municipal evictions.
* Grassroots Patronage: He has served as a primary political patron for the city's street-level traders, organizing rallies to demand "hawker-friendly" urban policies and acting as a mediator with city authorities.
Philanthropy and Social Contribution
Following his family's 250-year tradition of local leadership, Patwary has been involved in significant charitable activities:
* Educational Endowment: He established the Success Coaching Center and provided financial backing for the Tejgaon Law College, focusing on rural legal education.
* Religious and Social Infrastructure: As a descendant of the Rupsha Jamidar Bari, he has funded the maintenance of historical religious sites and local mosques as part of his Talukdar heritage.
Personal Life
He was married to Professor Advocate B.M. Khaleda Kabir, a senior lawyer of the Supreme Court of Bangladesh
